items.s0825: Explain what an "adversarial example" is. Give a concrete everyday example where this could be dangerous.
items.s0826: An adversarial example is an input (e.g. an image or text) that looks completely normal to a human, but through invisible deliberate changes (e.g. a few pixels) causes an AI system to make a completely wrong decision. Example: A stop sign with barely visible stickers is not recognized as a stop sign by the camera of a self-driving car, which can cause an accident.
items.s0827: What advantages does using AI in cybersecurity offer compared to classical rule-based systems?
items.s0828: AI can detect new, previously unknown attack patterns that are not in any rule database (so-called zero-day attacks). It learns from past attacks and improves automatically. AI can analyze huge amounts of data in real time, which would be impossible for humans alone. Classical systems can only detect what they were explicitly programmed to recognize.
items.s0829: What is an "AI-assisted social engineering attack"? Explain how schools and young people can protect themselves against it.
items.s0830: An AI-assisted social engineering attack uses AI to create fake, highly convincing messages, calls, or videos intended to manipulate victims (e.g. fake messages from the school principal). Protection: Never click on suspicious links, always confirm the sender through a second channel (e.g. phone call), train critical thinking, and immediately report suspicious messages to an adult.

items.s2647: What does the term "Instrumental Convergence" mean for a superintelligence? Give one example.
items.s2648: Instrumental convergence means that a superintelligence with almost any goal will pursue certain intermediate sub-goals useful for achieving its final objective. For example, it will try to prevent its own shutdown in order to keep pursuing the goal.
items.s2649: Briefly explain what an "Oracle AI" is and what advantage it might have over an autonomous superintelligence from a safety perspective.
items.s2650: An Oracle AI is a superintelligence that only answers questions but cannot take independent actions in the world. From a safety perspective, this is advantageous because a purely passive AI cannot implement its own plans or independently control resources.
items.s2651: What is referred to as "Takeoff Speed" in the emergence of a superintelligence, and why is this concept important for safety research?
items.s2652: Takeoff speed describes how quickly an AI rises from the human level to superintelligence. In a fast takeoff (Hard Takeoff), humans have no time to intervene, which makes safety research especially important for solving problems in advance.
items.s2653: Name two specific international initiatives or agreements that try to regulate the development of superintelligence at an international level.
